name: read_file
description:
Read content from one of your personal files.

Usage:
- Use this when you need to recall information: what you know about the other person, your current goals, or your relationships.
- The path must be relative to your personal directory. Examples: "knowledge/对方名.txt", "goals/current.txt", "relationships/某人.txt"
- Use line_start and line_count to read only what you need.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative file path within your character directory, e.g. "knowledge/对方名.txt"

parameters.name: line_start
parameters.description: Line number to start reading from (1-based). Omit to read from the beginning.

parameters.name: line_count
parameters.description: Number of lines to read. Omit to read to the end.

name: append_file
description:
Append new information to one of your personal files.

Usage:
- Use this when you learn something new about the other person: their identity, background, intentions, or opinions.
- Only write to files in your personal directory.
- Do NOT overwrite — new information is always appended, never replaced.
- The content should be a single concise sentence in Chinese.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A single sentence to append, in Chinese.

name: list_dir
description:
List files and directories within your personal directory.

Usage:
- Use this to discover what files you have (e.g., who you have relationship files for, what knowledge files exist).
- The path is relative to your character directory. Use "" for root.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative path to list, e.g. "" for root, "knowledge" for knowledge folder.

name: grep
description:
Search your personal files and world files for a keyword or phrase.

Usage:
- Use this before calling read_file — to find which files contain information you need and which lines to read.
- The pattern parameter is the keyword or phrase to search for (e.g., a person's name, a place, a topic).
- The path parameter (optional) limits the search scope. Use "knowledge", "chat_logs", "relationships", "goals", "decisions", "mailbox", "World", or leave empty for all.
- Returns each match as: file_path:line_number: matching line content.
- This lets you pinpoint exactly which file and line to read, rather than guessing.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The keyword or phrase to search for.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Subdirectory or file to limit search to. "knowledge", "chat_logs", "relationships", etc. "World" for world files. Empty or omitted for all of your directory.

name: write_file
description:
Create a new file or overwrite an existing one entirely.

Usage:
- Use this to create a new record from scratch or replace all content in a file.
- The content replaces the entire file — use edit_file if you only need to change part of a file.
- Do NOT write to chat_logs/ or persona.txt.
- The path is relative to your personal directory.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Full content to write to the file.

name: glob
description:
Find files in your personal directory matching a pattern.

Usage:
- Use this to discover files by name pattern, e.g. "knowledge/*.txt" to list all knowledge files, or "goals/*" to find all goals.
- The pattern supports * (match anything) and ? (match one character).
- Returns matching file paths relative to your directory.
- The pattern is relative to your personal directory. Use "World/*.txt" for world files.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Glob pattern, e.g. "knowledge/*.txt", "relationships/*", "goals/new_*". Supports * and ? wildcards.

name: edit_file
description:
Perform exact string replacement in one of your personal files.

Usage:
- Use this to UPDATE outdated information — e.g., when query_character reveals someone's status has changed, replace the stale record with current facts.
- The old_string must match EXACTLY one occurrence in the file. Include enough surrounding context to make it unique.
- The old_string is replaced with new_string in-place.
- Do NOT edit chat_logs (conversation records are immutable) or persona.txt.
- The path is relative to your personal directory.

parameters.name: old_string
parameters.description: The exact text to find and replace. Must match exactly one occurrence.

name: delete_file
description:
Delete one of your personal files.

Usage:
- Use this to remove obsolete records — completed goals, resolved decisions, outdated relationship notes.
- The path is relative to your personal directory.
- Do NOT delete chat_logs, persona.txt, or character.json.
- Deletion is permanent.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative file path to delete, e.g. "goals/old_plan.txt"

name: move_file
description:
Move or rename a file — useful for marking completed plans by moving them to a done/archive directory.

Usage:
- The old_path and new_path are both relative to your personal directory.
- Example: move_file("goals/plan_expand.txt", "goals/done_expand.txt")
- The target path must NOT already exist.
- This is equivalent to reading the file, writing it at the new path, then deleting the old.
- Do NOT move chat_logs, persona.txt, or character.json.

parameters.name: old_path
parameters.description: Current file path to move FROM.

parameters.name: new_path
parameters.description: New file path to move TO. Must not already exist.

name: send_letter
description:
Send a written letter to another entity. The letter will be delivered to their mailbox.

Usage:
- Call this when you need to communicate with someone who is not present — you are writing a letter, not speaking in person.
- The recipient will see your letter and may reply later.
- The content should be the full body of your letter, written in formal written style.

parameters.name: recipient_entity_id
parameters.description: The entity ID or Chinese name of the recipient. Use the [ID: xxx] shown in context if available, otherwise use the Chinese name (e.g. "拉盖娅").

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The full body of the letter in Chinese.
